title.value: Global Variations in Event-Based Surveillance for Disease Outbreak Detection: Time Series Analysis
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: Global Variations in Event-Based Surveillance for Disease Outbreak Detection: Time Series Analysis

extractions.description: The study assesses the variation in timing and frequency of event-based surveillance (EBS) reports compared to true outbreaks, using seasonal influenza epidemic in 24 countries as an example. It identifies factors influencing the variability in EBS performance.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on infectious disease surveillance and does not directly address sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Robust and flexible infectious disease surveillance is crucial for public health. Event-based surveillance (EBS) was developed to allow timely detection of infectious disease outbreaks by using mostly web-based data.

primary_category.justification: The paper is about disease outbreak detection and does not directly fall into any of the defined Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development categories.
primary_category.quote: The aim of this study was to assess the variation in the timing and frequency of EBS reports compared to true outbreaks and to identify the determinants of variability by using the example of seasonal influenza epidemic in 24 countries.
